paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend. The father in Proverbs 5 isn't just saying "don't." He's saying the sweet talk is a setup, because the forbidden woman's lips "drip honey" but "in the end she is bitter as wormwood" (Proverbs 5:3-4). That's the trick of sin: it shows you the honey first and hides the bill. So he tells his sons to "Keep your path far from her," and not even go near her door (Proverbs 5:8). I bet a lot of us know that if the cookie jar is on the counter, I'm not winning that fight.

Now hear the heart under the warning. The father isn't against joy, he's FOR it, and that's why he turns to a fountain, a loving doe and a wife of your youth (Proverbs 5:18-19). The warning protects something good. He says the same thing twice: don't hand your years and your wealth to strangers (Proverbs 5:9-10), and don't hate correction until you're groaning at the end (Proverbs 5:12-13). Listening to wise people early is cheaper than learning it late, and trust me, I'd know about learning things late.

And here's the part that should settle your heart. "A man's ways are before the eyes of the LORD, and the LORD examines all his paths" (Proverbs 5:21). Nobody is sneaking anything past Him, so the question is whether you'll let His wisdom lead you or let your own folly tie you up (Proverbs 5:22-23). So lean in, baker. Take the discipline, keep your path far from the trap, and stay faithful to what God has given you.
